⛵ Shore Excursion
Shipwreck & Turtle Cove
Dec 22 · 08:30
📖 Expand — Charlotte Amalie · St. Thomas
DestinationCharlotte Amalie curls around one of the loveliest natural harbors in the Caribbean — a horseshoe of green hills the Danes settled in the 1600s and never quite let go of. Their fingerprints are everywhere: the bright red walls of Fort Christian, the oldest standing structure on the island; the 99 Steps, a staircase laid with brick carried over as ship’s ballast from Denmark; and one of the oldest synagogues in the Western Hemisphere, its floor still laid in sand. Below runs Main Street, a duty-free warren of jewelers and rum shops, and beyond the town the water turns the impossible turquoise that made these islands famous.
Port InfoUnited States Virgin Islands · English · US dollar (USD) — no money to change, no passport line for U.S. guests. Warm and breezy in December. Ship berths alongside (Havensight / Crown Bay) — no tender. The Shipwreck & Turtle Cove snorkel departs by boat from the pier at 8:30 AM (about 3 hours).

⛵ Shore Excursion
River Tubing & Trafalgar Falls
Dec 23 · 11:00
📖 Expand — Roseau · Dominica
DestinationDominica is the Caribbean before the postcard — the “Nature Island,” a green wall of rainforest, hot springs and waterfalls that most cruisers only glimpse from the rail. Roseau, its small capital, is a lattice of French-colonial timber houses with fretwork balconies, a black-stone Gothic cathedral, and a Saturday market that spills with mangoes and root crops. Inland lies the headline: Morne Trois Pitons National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage rainforest where the Boiling Lake steams, hummingbirds hang in the mist, and the twin cascades of Trafalgar Falls drop into warm and cold pools side by side — the finish to your morning on the river.
Port InfoCommonwealth of Dominica · English · East Caribbean dollar (XCD); USD widely accepted. Hot and green in December. Ship berths alongside at the Roseau cruise berth — no tender. River Tubing & Trafalgar Falls departs 11:00 AM (about 4½ hours) — an active, feet-wet morning.

⛵ Shore Excursion
Dickenson Bay Beach Break
Dec 24 · 10:30
⛵ Shore Excursion
Catamaran Sunset Cruise
Dec 24 · 16:00
📖 Expand — St. John’s · Antigua
DestinationAntigua likes to claim a beach for every day of the year — 365 of them, pale and sheltered, ringed by the calmest water in the eastern Caribbean. Its capital, St. John’s, rises from the harbor in pastel clapboard beneath the white baroque towers of its cathedral; south of town lies Nelson’s Dockyard, the only working Georgian-era naval yard left in the world, where Horatio Nelson once careened his ships and the stone sail-lofts still stand around English Harbour. Dickenson Bay, on the calm northwest coast, is the island’s classic strand — soft sand, a gentle shelf, a rum punch never far — and by late afternoon the catamarans put out to trade the harbor lights for a Caribbean sunset.
Port InfoAntigua and Barbuda · English · East Caribbean dollar (XCD); USD accepted. Warm, dry trade-wind weather. Ship berths alongside (Heritage Quay, St. John’s) — no tender. Dickenson Bay Beach Break departs 10:30 AM; the Catamaran Sunset Cruise sails at 4:00 PM.

⛵ Shore Excursion
Foodie & Beach
Dec 25 · 10:30
📖 Expand — Basseterre · St. Kitts
DestinationSt. Kitts wears its history openly. Basseterre, the little grid-plan capital, gathers around The Circus — a Victorian roundabout with the green cast-iron Berkeley Memorial clock, modeled loosely on London’s Piccadilly — and the palm-lined Independence Square nearby, framed by the cathedral and Georgian townhouses. Above the old cane fields to the west stands Brimstone Hill Fortress, the “Gibraltar of the West Indies,” a UNESCO citadel with cannon still trained on the sea, while the dormant green cone of Mount Liamuiga shoulders the whole island. On Christmas Day your tour keeps it simple and warm: the flavors of the island, and a beach to ease into the holiday.
Port InfoSt. Kitts and Nevis · English · East Caribbean dollar (XCD); USD accepted. Warm and breezy in December. Ship berths alongside at Port Zante, Basseterre — no tender. Foodie & Beach departs 10:30 AM (about 4 hours). Being Christmas Day, some town shops will be closed — the beach and the tasting go on.

⛵ Shore Excursion
Escape to Jost Van Dyke
Dec 26 · 09:30
📖 Expand — Road Town · Tortola
DestinationTortola is the capital island of the British Virgin Islands and the undisputed sailing capital of the Caribbean — a ridge of green hills dropping to a hundred protected anchorages, its harbor a forest of masts. Road Town, the small colonial capital, has its botanic garden and its rum, but the day belongs to the water. Your excursion runs out to Jost Van Dyke, a separate island a short boat-ride north, barely four miles long and gloriously undeveloped: White Bay is a curve of talcum sand behind a reef, home to the legendary Soggy Dollar Bar — the sailors’ haunt said to have invented the Painkiller — where you wade ashore because there is no dock. It is the Caribbean stripped back to sand, rum and blue water, and a fitting last island before the sea days home.
Port InfoBritish Virgin Islands · English · US dollar (USD). Warm, dry December trades. The ship berths alongside at Road Town — no tender; the Jost Van Dyke excursion departs by boat at 9:30 AM (about 5 hours), with a wade-ashore beach landing.
